deltas.delta: No change in the interpreter source. The 14 core/vm files of OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master, core/state/statedb.go and transient_storage.go, Nitro master go.mod (holiman/uint256 v1.3.2, toolchain go1.25.12) and holiman/uint256 master mod.go and uint256.go fetched on 2026-11-27 are byte identical to the cycle 30 copies.

The newest public Nitro release is still v3.12.4 (960ca0a, release notes dated 2026-11-09, published 2026-11-19). Its notes and those of v3.12.1 to v3.12.3 change sequencer queueing, feed backfill, JSON-RPC argument checks and tracer memory, and touch no opcode, jump analysis, memory, storage or transient storage path. The rc.9 build that the endpoint reports is still unpublished.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on transaction boundaries or transient storage. Every early exit of StartTxHook on Nitro master runs no contract code, and every path that runs code passes StateDB.Prepare first, as cycles 1, 2 and 6 established.

No ArbOS upgrade is scheduled at block 527,957,324 (getScheduledUpgrade() returns zeros) and arbOSVersion() is 116 (ArbOS 61). The precompile at 0x100 returns empty data with success for the transfer and balanceOf shapes, as on Ethereum after Osaka; ArbSys and ArbRetryableTx revert on both.

The DAO network upgrades table still ends at ArbOS 61 Elara (Arbitrum One activation 2026-08-20), and the ArbOS releases overview names no later version. Priority fee collection with PGA ordering has been on since 23 September 2026 according to the ArbOS 61 notice. Ethereum's Glamsterdam has a Hoodi date of 15 December 2026 and no mainnet date; the approved Arbitrum change for it sets L1 pricing parameters only.

deltas.delta: Ethereum core developers set Glamsterdam on the Hoodi testnet for 15 December 2026 and kept EIP-8037 unchanged; mainnet is expected mid-January to May 2027. An ArbOS that adopts the Amsterdam rules dormant in Nitro v3.13.0 (F-145) would need a new Constitutional AIP, and none is posted.

Priority fee collection is enabled on Arbitrum One since 23 September 2026 together with PGA ordering, so transaction order inside a block follows the tip. This changes who wins ordering races; it does not change what a PoolManager call computes.

cleared.check: Cycle 32 rerun of battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py (250), pmdiff2.py (300), swaps.py, replay.py and callsem.py on the three official endpoints, with web3_clientVersion recorded before each stage.
cleared.result: Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain match on every vector, script and call semantics word. Elysium matches on everything except pmdiff2 script 189, which earlier cycles showed needs more than the 25 million gas the endpoint grants and equals Ethereum's record at 40 and 60 million. Robinhood Chain answered from both architectures (4 amd64 and 4 arm64 brackets), so both backends served parts of the run. Because the battery covers MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMPI, KECCAK256, MCOPY and CALLDATALOAD at the edges OPCODES.md lists, no line of FullMath.sol:21-54, TickMath, BitMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath or TickBitmap computes differently on these builds for those inputs.

cleared.result: 0 mismatches and 0 errors on both. cleared.result: Arbitrum One 5,832 swaps, Robinhood Chain 5,205 and Elysium 6,327 all satisfy the tick relation (no mismatch). Of the paired swaps (5,162, 4,329 and 5,809) every one is a single-step outcome or a multi-step swap. cleared.check: OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master core/vm (14 files), core/state statedb.go and transient_storage.go, Nitro master go.mod and holiman/uint256 master mod.go and uint256.go, refetched on 2026-11-27 and compared with the cycle 30 copies; Nitro release notes up to v3.12.4.
cleared.result: All files are byte identical to cycle 30. Nitro still pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 and go1.25.12. No public release after v3.12.4 exists, and the v3.12.1 to v3.12.4 notes change no interpreter, arithmetic, jump analysis, memory, storage or transient storage path.

cleared.check: Nitro master state_transition.go execute() and arbos/tx_processor.go StartTxHook, read again for any transaction type that runs contract code before StateDB.Prepare resets transient storage.
cleared.result: execute() returns at once when StartTxHook sets endTxNow (state_transition.go:635-646) and calls Prepare only later (line 736). The early-exit cases are deposits, internal transactions and retryable submissions; the deposit branch states that it does not invoke the EVM and only mints and transfers (tx_processor.go:260-268), the internal branch applies ArbOS updates (270-275), and the submission branch moves balances with TransferBalance. Retry transactions return false from the hook and take the normal path through Prepare. So the Lock flag, NonzeroDeltaCount, CurrencyDelta and the synced currency (src/libraries/Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol) start empty for every transaction that can call the PoolManager. This repeats the cycle 1, 2 and 6 result on today's master.

cleared.check: What the PoolManager's take and sync shapes do against the P256VERIFY precompile at 0x100, ArbSys (0x64) and ArbRetryableTx (0x6e), called from the PoolManager address by eth_call.
cleared.result: 0x100 returns success with empty data for both transfer(address,uint256) and balanceOf(address); 0x64 and 0x6e revert with empty data for both. For a currency of 0x100, take passes the success check of src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 because return data is empty, but no value leaves the PoolManager and the caller is debited the full amount in that currency (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). sync reverts because the high-level balanceOf call in Currency.sol:94 cannot decode empty return data, so no credit can be created in that currency by settle (PoolManager.sol:349-365). Ethereum has the same precompile at the same address since Osaka, so this is no difference from Ethereum. A pool naming such a currency is in the class of an attacker-chosen token and holds no value of other users.

cleared.check: ArbOS state on 2026-11-27: getScheduledUpgrade, arbOSVersion, getTransactionFilteringFrom, getNativeTokenManagementFrom, getMultiGasPricingConstraints, ArbWasm stylusVersion, and the PoolManager code length.
cleared.result: No upgrade is scheduled on any of the three; all report ArbOS 61 (116). Filtering is active only on Robinhood Chain (F-001). Native token management and multi-dimensional pricing are off. stylusVersion is 3 on all three. Each PoolManager still has 24,009 bytes of code.

cleared.check: Upgrades scheduled or proposed for the next six months and their effect on the PoolManager and on funds already inside it.
cleared.result: None is scheduled on chain. The DAO table ends at ArbOS 61. The approved Glamsterdam change for Arbitrum One sets parentGasFloorPerToken and perBatchGasCharge, which change only the L1 fee of a transaction. Ethereum Glamsterdam itself (Hoodi 15 December 2026, mainnet not before mid-January 2027) changes gas on the parent chain, where the PoolManager does not run; it can change gas for withdrawals through the bridge contracts, not what the PoolManager computes. If a later ArbOS enables the Amsterdam rules dormant in Nitro v3.13.0, the effect on the PoolManager is the one F-145 describes (gas reservoir only, no reinterpreted instruction). The Elysium upgrade of F-158 is still undated. An ordinary account gains no new action on any of these.

leadResults.answer: No Kinetiq image or binary for the mainnet build was found. Kinetiq's page (updated 25 November 2026) says only stock ArbOS 61 operated with Conduit. The one published Elysium node package (Enigma-Validator/elysium-rpc-node, by Hypedexer) targets testnet 99801 on offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.9.5-66e42c4. Conduit's mainnet RPC answers the same nitro/vlocal go1.25.12 string as the official endpoint, so the build appears to be Conduit's. In place of a lift, the battery and targeted sets were run on Conduit's endpoint and on dRPC with no mismatch (raw/alt_endpoints.json). A new lead asks for Conduit's image.

Still no public statement of the sequencer build. On 2026-11-27 the official endpoint answered rc.9 b72783f on amd64 and arm64 in equal parts, PublicNode answers a modified v3.12.2 snapshot, and dRPC hides its backend. Mined evidence stays the check: 5,205 new swaps satisfy the tick relation and 25 multi-step swaps replay to the unit.

Arbitrum One half only, again. Of eleven public endpoints tried on 2026-11-27 for debug_traceTransaction of failed transaction 0x04ac7750...3aba, only the Pocket gateway answered, and it reports nitro v3.12.4+960ca0a, the build already used. dRPC has no historical state, PublicNode, meowrpc and Blast refuse the method, Nodies needs a paid plan, Tenderly was rate limited twice, and three endpoints did not answer (raw/l1059_probe.txt). No second build is reachable without a key.
